input.question: Is there evidence that incest leads to genetic deformities? If so, how was it tested? What was the sample size / p-value / confidence interval? Was the claim held up to less scrutiny because this is a common belief?
input.ground_truth: We actually know a lot about inbreeding do to its importance in laboratory test animals and agriculture. The reason incest leads to genetic deformities is that those genes are usually recessive and they can only appear if the mother and father both possess the gene. Obviously related individuals are for likely to share the same negative recessive genes. I'm on mobile so I can't find exact studies but hopefully someone else can point you in the right direction.

Okay, let’s break it down in a way a 5-year-old can understand:

Imagine you have a big family tree with lots of cousins and uncles and aunts. If people who are very closely related (like siblings or a parent and child) have a baby, sometimes the baby can have health problems. Scientists have looked at this to see if it’s true.

How did they test it? They looked at families where this happened and checked if the babies had more health problems than in families where people weren’t closely related.

They studied a bunch of families—let’s say they looked at hundreds or even thousands of families to make sure they got a good answer. They use numbers called “p-values” and “confidence intervals” to see if the difference is real and not just by chance.

But sometimes, people already believe something (like “close family having babies is bad”) before the science is done, so they might not check as carefully. But good scientists still try to be careful and use numbers to make sure.

So, yes, there is some evidence that babies born to very closely related people can have more health problems, but it’s not super common because it doesn’t happen very often. Scientists did studies with big groups of people to find out.
